newsitem.title: USA: Conrail has profit in 4th quarter after year-ago loss.
newsitem.headline: Conrail has profit in 4th quarter after year-ago loss.

text.p: Conrail, the rail freight carrier that has been embroiled in a lengthy takeover squabble, Wednesday reported a profit for its fourth quarter and all of 1996.
"Though we began the year with one of the harshest winters on record, we finished 1996 on a very strong note," said David M. LeVan, Conrail's chairman, president and chief executive officer.
"This is the third consecutive quarter that we produced record results in net income, earnings per share and operating ratio," he said in a statement.
Conrail had fourth-quarter income of $147 million, or $1.86 per share, compared with a loss of $30 million, or 43 cents a share, in the fourth quarter of 1995.
For the full year, net income climbed to $342 million, or $4.25 per share, from $264 million, or $3.19 per share, for 1995.

The company added that despite the potential for distractions resulting from its proposed merger with CSX Corp. and the challenge mounted by Norfolk Southern, "our people clearly focused on controlling costs, improving safety, and maintaining high levels of service to our customers."
Revenues for the quarter were $943 million, down from $951 million a year earlier. For the year, revenues were $3.71 billion, up from $3.69 billion in 1995.
Conrail's stock rose $3.125 to close at $107.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
